Home page of James Cowden, an indie, songwriter artist from Scottsdale. There is an expansive hole in the music market that has left many with a thirst for music that touches with creativity , depth, inspiration and renewed passion. The music industry is not focused on generations of people who cannot connect emotionally or intellectually with pop, rap, and the latest retread of a boyband.  James prefers to offer new music that reflects experience (and how it’s presented) and allows this group to connect to themselves and their own gloriously complex worlds of experience.
Circuitous routes are part of artistic life and James' journey has been no less. 
After a series of life altering events, the gravitational pull of music was too strong and he made the leap of faith.  "I can honestly say music saved my life..."
As a solo performer... he has strong credentials having played in such well known venues as EDDIE'S ATTIC in Atlanta, LESTAT'S in San Diego as well a many European venues. His nomadic upbringing has served him well. Calling New Orleans his "spiritual home", the years living there had a tremendous formative effect. There is a sense of experience in his voice seldom encountered that draws the listener in to each song's deeper levels. A change of rhythm, a tweak of key bring a freshness to the music. As former lead vocalist for the Arizona based show band THE GROOVE MERCHANTS, James has a strong vocal presence not to be missed.

The first program is Contrology Coach. It is 8 weeks of 50 minute weekly meetings and semi-weekly private lessons. It is for Classically Trained or Classically Curious Teachers who want to focus equally on their own practice and their teaching.

The second program is called Contrology Club. It is 8 weeks of 80 minute weekly meetings. It is for Classically trained teachers (or those who have gone through a term of Contrology Coach) who want to dive into the system. Each week, we examine an exercise or two, diving into who it is for, some of the goals or benefits and explore how the system (ie both the exercises and apparatus) help to build, progress and challenge this exercise.

The third program is a monthly meeting series called Collective Sessions. These are 90 minute collaborative explorations into themes, exercises or common challenges we all face as Pilates Teachers.
